overview: Autophagy is the cell recycling its own components to survive stress; apoptosis is the cell's programmed decision to die entirely.
genZNote: Autophagy: cell doing spring cleaning to survive. Apoptosis: cell deciding it's time to go.

aspects.label: Outcome for the Cell
aspects.valueA: The cell survives, having recycled damaged components for energy and building blocks.
aspects.valueB: The cell dies in a controlled, organised manner.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Damaged organelles/proteins are engulfed by autophagosomes and degraded in lysosomes.
aspects.valueB: Caspase enzymes are activated, breaking down the cell in a controlled cascade.

aspects.label: Typical Trigger
aspects.valueB: Developmental signals, DNA damage, or immune instructions.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Excessive or dysregulated autophagy can itself sometimes trigger apoptosis — the two pathways can interact.
overlay.memoryTrick: Auto (self) + phagy (eating) = eating your own parts to survive. Apoptosis = 'falling away', i.e. dying.
overlay.commonMisconception: Autophagy is not a form of cell death by default — it's primarily a survival mechanism, though it can occasionally contribute to a form of programmed cell death in extreme cases.
